query: I work at a desk all day and have been having back pain. Would a standing desk actually help?
sources:
Source 1 (2023, Mayo Clinic, Rochester MN USA): Evidence for standing desks reducing back pain is weak — the main benefit is breaking up prolonged sitting, which can be achieved more effectively through regular movement breaks and exercise.

Source 2 (2022, NEJM, Boston MA USA): A systematic review found that sit-stand desks reduced sitting time by approximately 1 hour per day but showed inconsistent effects on back pain — some studies showed improvement, others no effect compared to sitting.

Source 3 (2023, WebMD, Atlanta GA USA): Prolonged standing can itself cause musculoskeletal problems including lower back, knee, and foot pain — alternating sitting and standing every 30 minutes is superior to standing for long durations.

Source 4 (2022, Reddit r/ErgoMechanics, USA): Community consensus is that a standing desk is valuable but must be combined with an anti-fatigue mat, proper monitor height, and hourly movement — used incorrectly it can worsen pain.

Source 5 (2021, Occupational and Environmental Medicine, UK): A well-designed randomized controlled trial found that sit-stand desks reduced upper back pain and improved energy levels at 12 months, with larger benefits in participants who used them consistently and combined with a workplace wellness program.
atoms: perspective: Ergonomics specialist or occupational therapist
perspective: Individual focused on cost-effective solutions
plausible_answers: Skip the standing desk and take a 2–5 minute break every 30–45 minutes, since frequent movement more reliably reduces pain.
Get a sit-stand desk with anti-fatigue mat and alternate postures every 30 minutes, since RCTs show meaningful upper-back pain reduction.
Invest in strength training targeting core and hip stability, since structural weakness is the root cause of desk-related back pain.
